positions.name: AsyncJobContractDispatch
positions.frame: what does the async job contract guarantee when remember dispatches — return latency, work-loss risk, and how the extraction gets tracked afterward?
positions.why: All three expressions describe the same ratified async mechanism from complementary angles: src-1 declares the contract itself (receipt returned, cursor-polled extraction), src-2 asserts its operational guarantees (non-blocking, no lost work), and src-3 — spoken by a different participant, framed explicitly as a 'Key decision' — restates the same dispatch with its poll-or-piggyback branching. The register direction (technical, native-jargon) and conviction direction (decision-grade in both src-1 and src-3) run consistent across all three even though the speakers differ, which is what licenses reading them as one contract-shaped group rather than three isolated remarks. The held tension: src-1/src-2 report the contract as already-settled fact, while src-3 performs the settling itself as a live 'Key decision' — the frame holds both readings without resolving which act was primary.
